prompt: Country A and Country B have identical PPCs (both linear: max 400 wheat or 400 steel). An economist argues there are no gains from trade between them. Is this correct, and why?

options.label: A
options.text: Incorrect — identical PPCs always create gains from trade

options.label: B
options.text: Correct — if both countries have identical PPCs, their opportunity costs are equal. There is no comparative advantage, no reason to specialize differently, and therefore no gains from trade through specialization

options.label: C
options.text: Incorrect — gains from trade depend on absolute advantage, not opportunity costs

options.label: D
options.text: Correct — but only if both countries have the same population size

options.label: E
options.text: Incorrect — identical PPCs allow trade at fixed terms that benefit both

explanation: If both countries have identical linear PPCs, their opportunity costs are equal (e.g., both face OC of wheat = 1 steel).
